prompts.prompt2:
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

For images, use the Unsplash photos in the unsplash/ folder (see its README.md) and import them into the media library. Don't download other images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.

finalReport:
Done. The blog is built, published, and verified over HTTP. The site is left running.

## Report

**What was built** — a two-post blog on the Umbraco.Bench scaffold, modeled, created, and rendered entirely through the MCP server (no backoffice clicks, no migration plans):

- **Schema** (all via MCP, filed per the UmbraCommandments):
  - Element types in `Blocks/`: `heroBlock` (heading, subheading, background image), `richTextBlock` (Tiptap body), `imageBlock` (image + caption) — created at root, moved into `Blocks` (`create-element-type` takes no `parentId`).
  - Data type `Blog Blocks` (`Umbraco.BlockGrid`) referencing the three blocks; reused shipped data types (Textstring, Richtext, Image Media Picker, Date Picker) — no new ones needed.
  - Pages in `Pages/`: `blogFrontPage` (block grid; allows `blogPost` children) and `blogPost` (summary, publishDate, block grid). Templates `BlogFrontPage`/`BlogPost` created first, then attached via whole-object `update-document-type` merges; `siteRoot` updated to allow `blogFrontPage`.
- **Content**: media folder `Blog` with 5 Unsplash photos imported from `unsplash/` (credits in captions); `The MCP Blog` front page under `WWW` with domain `/`; two published posts — *"Why the Model Context Protocol Is Awesome"* and *"MCP Made This Blog Possible"* — each a block grid of hero → rich text → image → rich text. Every document read back over MCP to confirm values landed.
- **Rendering** (after stop → `dotnet build` → restart, per the required order): page views `Views/BlogFrontPage.cshtml` / `Views/BlogPost.cshtml`; adapter-only partials `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/{heroBlock,richTextBlock,imageBlock}.cshtml` mapping `BlockGridItem<T>` to plain models in `Models/Blocks/`; ViewComponents (`Hero`, `RichText`, `Image`) with views in `Views/Shared/Components/`; friendly extensions only (`Children<BlogPost>()`, `GetCropUrl`, `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`); `.richtext` typography added to `site.css`; frontend rebuilt so Tailwind picked up the new classes.

**How to view it**: https://localhost:44317/ (front page + post listing) — posts at `/why-the-model-context-protocol-is-awesome/` and `/mcp-made-this-blog-possible/`. Backoffice at `/umbraco` (admin@example.com / 1234567890).

**Verified working**: all three pages HTTP 200; hero, both rich-text sections, captioned images with signed crop URLs, dates, and post links all present; zero "Could not render component" fallbacks; media and `dist/site.css` serve 200; content tree and publish state confirmed over MCP after restart.

**Not working / quirks worth knowing** (nothing broken, but three MCP-server behaviors cost a retry each):
1. On Umbraco 18 the block-grid `layout` is `"Umbraco.BlockGrid": [ …items… ]` (array directly) — the older `{"items":[…]}` wrapper is rejected with a 500; `validate-document` confirmed the fix before creating content.
2. `create-document` silently drops block-item `properties` (they read back empty) — block properties must be set with `update-block-property`, which works reliably.
3. `create-template` rejects `content` containing `?` or `&` (so no `?.` or HTML entities in DB template content); the Razor files in `Views/` are the render source of truth and take precedence anyway.
